subject: maths
title: Money: Coins and Notes, Pounds and Pence
seo_title: Year 1 Money Worksheets: UK Coins and Notes, Pounds and Pence
standard_text: Recognise and know the value of different denominations of coins and notes.
meta_desc: Free Year 1 maths worksheets on money: name UK coins and notes, find which is worth more (a 2p coin is bigger but 5p is worth more), tell pounds from pence, count coins up to 20p and shop in the class shop. 100 questions with an answer key, following the National Curriculum.
key_big: Read the number on the coin, not its size.
key_sub: p means pence and £ means pounds. A 5p coin is worth more than a bigger 2p coin, and £1 is 100p. Count coins starting with the one worth the most.
body_html:
Coins and notes

We pay with coins and notes. Each one shows its value. p means pence. £ means pounds.

Read the number, not the size

A big coin is not always worth more. The 2p coin is bigger than the 5p coin, but 5p is worth more.

£1 is worth 100p. So a £1 coin is worth much more than a 1p coin.

Count the coins, biggest first

Start with the coin worth the most. Then count on.

Example

A lolly costs 8p. You have a 10p coin. Can you buy it?

10p is more than 8p.

Answer: Yes

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
The 2p coin is bigger, so it is worth more than 5pRead the number on the coin: 5p is more than 2p
3 coins, so 3pAdd the value of each coin: 10p, 15p, 17p
£1 is the same as 1p£1 = 100p, so £1 is worth much more

faq.q: What money does a Year 1 child need to know?
faq.a: In the National Curriculum, Year 1 pupils recognise and know the value of all the UK coins (1p, 2p, 5p, 10p, 20p, 50p, £1, £2) and notes (£5, £10, £20).

faq.q: Why is a 2p coin bigger than a 5p coin?
faq.a: The size of a coin does not show its value. Children need to read the number on the coin: 5p is worth more than 2p, even though it is smaller.

faq.q: What is the difference between pounds and pence?
faq.a: £ means pounds and p means pence. There are 100 pence in £1, so a £1 coin is worth much more than a 1p coin.

faq.q: How can I help my child learn about money at home?
faq.a: Let them sort real coins, find the one worth the most, and play shop with prices up to 20p. Ask them to count the coins starting with the biggest value.

items.q: What is this coin?
items.e: It is the 1p coin (one penny). The p means pence.

items.q: What is this coin?
items.e: It is the 2p coin (two pence). The p means pence.

items.q: What is this coin?
items.e: It is the 5p coin (five pence). The p means pence.

items.q: What is this coin?
items.e: It is the 10p coin (ten pence). The p means pence.

items.q: What is this coin?
items.e: It is the 20p coin (twenty pence). The p means pence.

items.q: What is this coin?
items.e: It is the 50p coin (fifty pence). The p means pence.

items.q: What is this coin?
items.e: It is the £1 coin (one pound). The £ sign means pounds.

items.q: What is this coin?
items.e: It is the £2 coin (two pounds). The £ sign means pounds.

items.q: What is this note?
items.e: It is the £5 note (five pounds). A note is flat. Coins are made of metal.

items.q: What is this note?
items.e: It is the £10 note (ten pounds). A note is flat. Coins are made of metal.

items.q: What is this note?
items.e: It is the £20 note (twenty pounds). A note is flat. Coins are made of metal.

items.q: Which one is a note?
items.e: B is the £5 note. The others are coins. A note is a flat rectangle you can fold.

items.q: Which one is a note?
items.e: B is the £10 note. 10p is a coin, not a note.

items.q: Which one is a coin?
items.e: D is the £2 coin. The others are notes.

items.q: Find the 50p coin.
items.e: D says 50p. The 5p coin is much smaller and worth much less.

items.q: Find the 2p coin.
items.e: A says 2p. 20p and £2 also have a 2 in them, but they are different coins.

items.q: Find the £1 coin.
items.e: B says £1. The £ sign comes first. 1p is a penny, not a pound.

items.q: Count the sides of the 50p coin. How many sides does it have?
items.e: Count round the edge: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. The 50p coin has 7 sides. The 20p coin has 7 sides too.

items.q: This coin has 12 sides. It is gold and silver. Which coin is it?
items.e: The £1 coin has 12 sides. The 20p and 50p coins have 7 sides. The £2 coin is round.

items.q: Which one means “two pence”?
items.e: Pence are written with a p after the number: 2p. £2 means two pounds.

items.q: Which is worth more?
items.e: 10p is worth more than 2p, so the answer is 10p. The 2p coin is bigger, but size does not show the value. Read the number.

items.q: Which is worth more?
items.e: 5p is worth more than 2p, so the answer is 5p. The 2p coin is bigger, but size does not show the value. Read the number.

items.q: Which is worth more?
items.e: £1 is worth more than 50p, so the answer is £1. The 50p coin is bigger, but size does not show the value. Read the number.

items.q: Which is worth more?
items.e: 20p is worth more than 10p, so the answer is 20p. The 10p coin is bigger, but size does not show the value. Read the number.

items.q: Which is worth more?
items.e: 50p is worth more than 20p, so the answer is 50p.

items.q: Which is worth less?
items.e: 5p is worth more than 1p, so the answer is 1p. The 1p coin is bigger, but size does not show the value. Read the number.

items.q: Which is worth more?
items.e: £10 is worth more than £2, so the answer is £10.

items.q: Which is worth less?
items.e: 20p is worth more than 5p, so the answer is 5p.

items.q: Which is worth more?
items.e: £20 is worth more than £10, so the answer is £20.

items.q: Which is worth less?
items.e: £2 is worth more than 50p, so the answer is 50p. £2 is 200p, so it is worth more.

items.q: Which is worth less?
items.e: £5 is worth more than £2, so the answer is £2.

items.q: Which is worth less?
items.e: £1 is worth more than 20p, so the answer is 20p. £1 is 100p, so it is worth more.

items.q: Which is worth the most?
items.e: 10p is worth the most, so it is B. The 2p coin is bigger, but 2p is less than 10p.

items.q: Which is worth the most?
items.e: £1 is worth the most, so it is A. The 50p coin is bigger, but £1 = 100p.

items.q: Which is worth the least?
items.e: 2p is worth the least, so it is C. The 5p coin is smaller, but 5p is more than 2p.

items.q: Which is worth the least?
items.e: 20p is worth the least, so it is B.

items.q: Which is worth the most?
items.e: The £5 note is worth the most, so it is B. £5 is more than £2.

items.q: Put the coins in order. Start with the one worth the least: 10p, 2p, 5p.
items.e: Look at the numbers, not the sizes: 2 is less than 5, and 5 is less than 10. So: 2p, 5p, 10p. 5p, 10p, 2p is the order of size (smallest coin first).

items.q: Which is worth more: one £1 coin or three 10p coins?
items.e: Three 10p coins make 10p, 20p, 30p. £1 is 100p, so one £1 coin is worth more. More coins does not mean more money.

items.q: Which is worth more: one 10p coin or five 1p coins?
items.e: Five 1p coins make 5p. 10p is more than 5p, so one 10p coin is worth more.

items.q: This coin is worth 2 ___.
items.e: It says 2p. The p means pence, so it is 2 pence.

items.q: This coin is worth 2 ___.
items.e: It says £2. The £ sign means pounds, so it is 2 pounds.

items.q: This coin is worth 50 ___.
items.e: It says 50p. The p means pence, so it is 50 pence.

items.q: This note is worth 5 ___.
items.e: It says £5. The £ sign means pounds, so it is 5 pounds.

items.q: What does the £ sign mean?
items.e: £ means pounds. £3 is three pounds.

items.q: What does the p in 20p mean?
items.e: p means pence. 20p is twenty pence.

items.q: How many pence make £1?
items.e: 100p make £1. So £1 is worth much more than 1p.

items.q: How do you write two pounds?
items.e: Write the £ sign first, then the number: £2. 2p is two pence.

items.q: How do you write fifty pence?
items.e: Write the number, then p: 50p.

items.q: How do you write ten pounds?
items.e: The £ sign goes before the number: £10.

items.q: Which coins are all pence coins?
items.e: Pence coins have a p: 1p, 2p, 5p, 10p, 20p and 50p. So 1p, 5p, 20p.

items.q: Which are all pounds?
items.e: Pounds have the £ sign: £1 and £2 coins, and £5, £10 and £20 notes. So £1, £2, £5.

items.q: Which one is worth pence, not pounds?
items.e: C is 20p. It has a p, so it is pence. The others have the £ sign.

items.q: Which one is worth pounds?
items.e: A is £2. It has the £ sign, so it is pounds. 50p is pence.

items.q: How many 1p coins make 10p?
items.e: Count in 1s: 1p, 2p, 3p … 10p. That is 10 coins. One 1p coin is only 1p.

items.q: Which is worth more: £2 or 20p?
items.e: £2 is pounds: £2 = 200p. 20p is only 20 pence. So £2 is worth more.

items.q: Which is worth more: £5 or 50p?
items.e: £5 is pounds: £5 = 500p. 50p is only 50 pence. So £5 is worth more.

items.q: Which is worth more: £10 or 10p?
items.e: £10 is pounds: £10 = 1,000p. 10p is only 10 pence. So £10 is worth more.

items.q: Isla has a £1 coin. Jack has a 1p coin. Do they have the same amount?
items.e: £1 is one pound = 100p. 1p is one penny. No. £1 is more.

items.q: Alfie has three coins: £1, £2 and 20p. How many are pound coins?
items.e: £1 and £2 have the £ sign. 20p is pence. So 2 are pound coins.

items.q: How much money is this?
items.e: Each coin is 1p. Count: 1p, 2p, 3p, 4p. That is 4p. Count the value of each coin, not the number of coins.

items.q: Grace has these coins. How much does she have?
items.e: Each coin is 2p. Count in 2s: 2p, 4p, 6p. That is 6p. Count the value of each coin, not the number of coins.

items.q: Mohammed finds these coins in his pocket. How much is it?
items.e: Each coin is 5p. Count in 5s: 5p, 10p. That is 10p. Count the value of each coin, not the number of coins.

items.q: What is the total?
items.e: Each coin is 10p. Count in 10s: 10p, 20p. That is 20p. Count the value of each coin, not the number of coins.

items.q: Oliver puts these coins in a money box. How much is in the box?
items.e: Each coin is 2p. Count in 2s: 2p, 4p, 6p, 8p, 10p. That is 10p. Count the value of each coin, not the number of coins.

items.q: How much money is this?
items.e: Each coin is 5p. Count in 5s: 5p, 10p, 15p. That is 15p. Count the value of each coin, not the number of coins.

items.q: Lily has these coins. How much does she have?
items.e: Start with the biggest coin: 10p, 15p. That is 15p.

items.q: Ruby finds these coins in her pocket. How much is it?
items.e: Start with the biggest coin: 10p, 12p. That is 12p.

items.q: What is the total?
items.e: Start with the biggest coin: 5p, 6p, 7p. That is 7p.

items.q: George puts these coins in a money box. How much is in the box?
items.e: Start with the biggest coin: 5p, 7p, 8p. That is 8p.

items.q: How much money is this?
items.e: Start with the biggest coin: 10p, 12p, 14p. That is 14p.

items.q: Amelia has these coins. How much does she have?
items.e: Start with the biggest coin: 10p, 11p, 12p, 13p. That is 13p. Count the value of each coin, not the number of coins.

items.q: Freya finds these coins in her pocket. How much is it?
items.e: Start with the biggest coin: 5p, 10p, 12p. That is 12p.

items.q: What is the total?
items.e: Put the coins in order, biggest value first. Start with the biggest coin: 10p, 15p, 16p. That is 16p.

items.q: Aisha puts these coins in a money box. How much is in the box?
items.e: Put the coins in order, biggest value first. Start with the biggest coin: 2p, 4p, 6p, 8p, 9p. That is 9p. Count the value of each coin, not the number of coins.

items.q: How much money is this?
items.e: Put the coins in order, biggest value first. Start with the biggest coin: 10p, 15p, 17p, 18p. That is 18p. Count the value of each coin, not the number of coins.

items.q: Maya has these coins. How much does she have?
items.e: Put the coins in order, biggest value first. Start with the biggest coin: 5p, 10p, 12p, 13p. That is 13p. Count the value of each coin, not the number of coins.

items.q: Which coins make 7p?
items.e: 5p + 2p = 7p, so the answer is 5p and 2p.

items.q: Which coins make 9p?
items.e: 5p + 2p + 2p = 9p, so the answer is 5p, 2p and 2p.

items.q: Which coins make 13p?
items.e: 10p + 2p + 1p = 13p, so the answer is 10p, 2p and 1p.

items.q: Ava has a 10p coin. A sweet costs 7p. Can she buy it?
items.e: 10p is more than 7p, so yes. One 10p coin is worth 10p, not 1p.

items.q: Kai has three 1p coins. Isla has one 5p coin. Who has more money?
items.e: Kai has 1p, 2p, 3p = 3p. Isla has 5p. 5p is more, so Isla. More coins does not mean more money.

items.q: Zara has one 10p coin. Jack has four 2p coins. Who has more money?
items.e: Jack has 2p, 4p, 6p, 8p = 8p. 10p is more than 8p, so Zara.

items.q: A pencil costs 5p. Alfie buys 2 pencils. How much does he pay?
items.e: 5p + 5p = 10p. 7p is 5 + 2, but 2 is the number of pencils, not pence.

items.q: A toy car costs 8p. Poppy pays with a 10p coin. How much change does she get?
items.e: Count on from 8p to 10p: 9p, 10p. That is 2 steps, so the change is 2p. Check: 8p + 2p = 10p.

items.q: Mohammed has a 5p coin and a 2p coin. A rubber costs 9p. How much more does he need?
items.e: Mohammed has 5p + 2p = 7p. Count on from 7p to 9p: 8p, 9p. He needs 2p more. 4p forgets the 2p coin.

items.q: A sticker costs 5p. Which coins make exactly 5p?
items.e: 2p + 2p + 1p = 5p, so 2p, 2p and 1p. 2p and 2p only make 4p.

items.q: Oliver has a £1 coin. A ball costs £2. Can he buy it?
items.e: £2 is more than £1, so no. Oliver needs one more pound.

items.q: A book costs £5. Lily has a £5 note. Can she buy it?
items.e: The note is worth £5 and the book costs £5. So yes. One note can be worth a lot.

items.q: In the class shop, Ruby buys an apple and a banana. How much does she pay?
items.e: Start with the bigger number: 6p, then count on 4: 7p, 8p, 9p, 10p. That is 10p. 2p is the difference, not the total.

items.q: In the class shop, Ethan buys a cake and an apple. How much does he pay?
items.e: 9p + 4p: count on from 9p: 10p, 11p, 12p, 13p. That is 13p.

items.q: Amelia has a 5p coin. Which one can she buy?
items.e: Only the apple costs less than 5p (4p). So Amelia can buy the apple.

items.q: Freya buys a banana. She pays with a 10p coin. How much change does she get?
items.e: Count on from 6p to 10p: 7p, 8p, 9p, 10p. That is 4 steps, so the change is 4p. 6p is the price, not the change.

items.q: Aisha has two 5p coins. Can she buy the cake?
items.e: 5p + 5p = 10p. The cake is 9p, and 10p is more than 9p. So yes.

items.q: Pencils cost 2p each. Arjun has 6p. How many pencils can he buy?
items.e: Count in 2s: 2p, 4p, 6p. That is 3 jumps, so 3 pencils.

items.q: Harry has 20p. He spends 10p on a toy. How much does he have left?
items.e: 20p take away 10p is 10p. 30p adds instead of taking away.

items.q: Kai has a 10p coin, a 5p coin and a 1p coin. How much money does he have?
items.e: Start with the biggest coin: 10p, 15p, 16p. That is 16p. 3p counts the coins, not their values.

items.q: Isla gets a £1 coin from Mum and a £2 coin from Gran. How much does she have now?
items.e: £1 + £2 = £3. These are pound coins, so it is £3, not 3p.

items.q: Jack has a £5 note and a £10 note. How much money does he have?
items.e: £10 + £5 = £15. £2 counts the notes, not their values.

items.q: Poppy has 12p. Mohammed has 15p. How much more does Mohammed have?
items.e: Count on from 12p to 15p: 13p, 14p, 15p. That is 3 steps, so Mohammed has 3p more.
